title: Dualizing tensor cocycle and normalized etale source locality
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes; absolute separatedness is not assumed. All morphisms below are separated and of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Every smooth morphism below is assumed to have a pure relative dimension $d_h\geq0$. Work in the bounded constructible finite-Tor categories [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and constructible exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Write $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$, take $c_{v,u}:R(vu)^!\simeq Ru^!Rv^!$ to be the specified adjunction conjugate of compact-support composition [def-pur-finite-exceptional-composition], and take $\theta_{h,M}$ and $\beta_{h,v}$ to be the specified counit transposes [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For composable smooth maps [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] put $\sigma_{u,v}=c_{v,u,\Lambda}^{-1}\theta_{u,\omega_v}\mathrm{sym}$. All pullback compositions, tensor constraints and unit comparisons below are the canonical derived ones [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].
For an etale map $e$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], use the counit-normalized comparison $\rho_e:Re^!\simeq Le^*$, its unit value $\eta_e:\omega_e\simeq\Lambda$, and $E_{e,h}=\rho_{e,\omega_h}c_{h,e,\Lambda}:\omega_{he}\simeq Le^*\omega_h$ [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization].
For every composable smooth triple $u:S\to X$, $v:X\to Y$, $w:Y\to Z$, the maps $\sigma$ are isomorphisms and satisfy
$$\sigma_{vu,w}(\sigma_{u,v}\otimes1)=\sigma_{u,wv}(1\otimes Lu^*\sigma_{v,w}).$$
If $u$ is etale, removing $\omega_u$ by $\eta_u$ gives
$$E_{u,wv}\sigma_{vu,w}=Lu^*\sigma_{v,w}(E_{u,v}\otimes1).$$
For a smooth Cartesian square $(h:X\to Y,h':X'\to Y',v:Y'\to Y,u:X'\to X)$ and an etale $e:X_1\to X$, let $X_1'=X_1\times_XX'$, with $e':X_1'\to X'$ and $u_1:X_1'\to X_1$. Then, with the same lower arrow $v$ in the base-change square for $he$,
$$E_{e',h'}\beta_{he,v}=Le'^*\beta_{h,v}\circ Lu_1^*E_{e,h}.$$
For a Cartesian base change of a smooth composable pair, the base-change comparisons intertwine $\sigma$ with the base-changed $\sigma$, including further open base changes. Consequently the canonical expressions built by finite composition, inverse, tensor product and derived pullback from $\beta$, $\sigma$ and the above $E$ commute with compatible restriction to opens in each scheme. Source-open comparisons in this assertion are $E$ for open immersions; they do not require a source-open square to be Cartesian. This assertion includes pullback along sections of the restricted diagrams.

proof.text:
Apply the tower formula of [lem-pur-smooth-exceptional-tensor-pasting] to the smooth tower $e:X_1\to X$, $h:X\to Y$, and its Cartesian pullback along $v$. Denote the upper arrows by $u_1,u$, as in the statement. It gives
$$\beta_{he,v}Lu_1^*\sigma_{e,h}=\sigma_{e',h'}(\beta_{e,u}\otimes Le'^*\beta_{h,v}).$$
The base change $e'$ is etale, and [lem-pur-finite-etale-dualizing-normalization] supplies
$$E_{e',h'}\sigma_{e',h'}=\eta_{e'}\otimes1,\qquad \eta_{e'}\beta_{e,u}=Lu_1^*\eta_e,\qquad E_{e,h}\sigma_{e,h}=\eta_e\otimes1.$$
Consequently postcomposing the preceding tower formula with $E_{e',h'}$ gives
$$E_{e',h'}\beta_{he,v}Lu_1^*\sigma_{e,h}=Le'^*\beta_{h,v}\,Lu_1^*(E_{e,h}\sigma_{e,h}).$$
The pullback $Lu_1^*\sigma_{e,h}$ is an isomorphism, so cancellation proves
$$E_{e',h'}\beta_{he,v}=Le'^*\beta_{h,v}\,Lu_1^*E_{e,h}.$$
In particular the lower arrow throughout this calculation is $v$, not the upper comparison $u$; no source-localization square has been declared Cartesian. In Lean a generic monoidal calculation moves eta through the tensor pullback comparison using its left naturality and left-unitor identity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-dualizing-primitive-open-restriction] for the three primitive open squares. Induct on RestrictionExpression: primitive constructors use these squares, identity uses functoriality, composition pastes squares, inverse cancels the mapped isomorphism, tensor uses naturality of the tensor-pullback isomorphism and derivedTensorHom_comp, and pullback uses naturality of pullSquare and the functor image of the induction equality. The last constructor permits arbitrary commuting pullback squares, including sections. Assemble the nine conjuncts.
